beats_top.query: cornell off campus meal plan or cook yourself cost
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2017 Sun article about a defunct private meal plan, so ours is more current and complete on plan prices. But the question is 'cook or buy a plan', and our page never gives a cooking cost: it admits it has no grocery basket and tells the student to build their own. The planned angle (three eating styles with a weekly basket) is not delivered, so a student still has to do the main comparison themselves.
changes: Add a sourced weekly and per-year cooking cost estimate (for example the USDA monthly food plan costs for a young adult; the writer must open and cite the current USDA Food Plans page) and compare it directly with each plan's per-year cost.

Add the three eating styles (cook nearly all, cook dinners and eat lunch on campus, eat on campus mostly) each with a total yearly cost using the plan prices plus the cooking estimate, in one small table.
Open with the answer and numbers: cooking-only estimate versus Just Bucks versus Off-Campus Value, instead of an admission that no grocery price was found.

fixes: Change the aid-office sentence in 'What the plans cost' to say the $7,604 food budget is the 2025-26 figure (source https://finaid.cornell.edu/cost-attend), or remove the claim that it matches 2026-27 Unlimited.

In 'The cooking side', delete 'and she judged cooking better value' and change 'she expected groceries plus eating out to total about $1,700 for the year' to say she estimated about $1,700 on groceries and dining out, timeframe not stated (source https://cornellsun.com/2020/10/26/a-skidmore-medal-topped-with-runny-pasta-freshman-year-with-zero-meal-plan).

Remove 'You can add or upgrade at any time, and charges are prorated weekly' from rule 1, or replace it with what https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/deadlines-terms says (students can sign up for a meal plan at any time) and drop the proration claim unless a Cornell page supports it.

Add an inline link to https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/undergraduate-meal-plans on rule 3 ('You must enroll in a plan before adding funds'), and inline links on rule 4 (debit carryover: terms page; BRB dates: undergraduate plans page for May 27 and the deadlines page for May 31).

State that the plans page does not say whether Bear Traditional and Unlimited are open to off-campus students (it lists eligibility only for Bear Choice, Bear Basic and the debit plans), or drop them from the 'off-campus' framing, and point the Bear Choice/Bear Basic recommendations to those confirmed-eligible plans.

Deliver the planned angle: add a cooking-cost estimate from an official source with a link (for example the USDA Food Plans monthly cost reports for the current month; open the page and record the figure and date) and a table of total yearly cost for three eating styles (cook nearly all; cook dinners and eat lunch on campus; eat on campus most days) using the 2026-27 plan prices already in the article. Label the estimate as ours and state the assumptions. Rewrite the first paragraph to give the cooking-only yearly estimate beside Just Bucks ($1,000) and Off-Campus Value ($1,824.60), and remove the 'we could not verify a retail grocery basket price' caveat from the opening.
